description:
Hi, I’m Tanzim, a full-stack web developer in St. John’s. I build web apps with JavaScript, TypeScript and React. I also enjoy UX design.

I am working on the astronaut health challenge. My goal is a simple app that helps astronauts check their own health and know what to do next.

I am working solo, but I am happy to chat and share ideas with anyone!
summary: Remote Doctor is an offline health app for astronauts on long missions, like a Mars trip where the doctor on Earth is up to 20 minutes away. Every day, the astronaut sees their "Ghost Self": a body map that shows how each part of their body is heading toward landing day. Weak parts fade. Tapping a part explains what it does, which spaceflight hazard affects it, and how it is measured in space. The app gives one clear action for today and an escalation level (self-care, crew medical officer, flight surgeon, or urgent protocol), plus what to do if Earth cannot answer. This addresses the challenge directly: astronauts must assess their own health and know when to get help, because real-time help from Earth is not possible.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

- Ghost Self body map: 9 clickable body parts (brain/mind, eyes, heart and vessels, blood/immune, muscles, bones, metabolism, sleep, radiation). Each shows status, trend, the NASA hazard behind it, how it is measured in space, a trend chart with a forecast to landing day, and what to do.

- Escalation levels 1-4: self-care, crew medical officer, flight surgeon (Earth), or urgent protocol. Findings are judged against the astronaut's own "space normal", over several days, with combined signs - never a single reading. Expected space changes (slightly higher temperature, lower blood pressure) do not cause false alarms.

- One Action: the single most important step for today, with "If Earth cannot answer" instructions. Uses real countermeasures, e.g. thigh cuffs for early SANS signs.

- 30-second morning check-in with NASA's suggested indicators (blood pressure, heart rate, blood sugar, temperature, sleep hours, mood) plus space-specific symptoms.

- "How to measure" guides, because astronauts should not be expected to know everything.

- Earth Report: daily and weekly reports wait in a queue and are sent at the next communication window. The flight surgeon's reply arrives after the real light-time delay.

- Roles and privacy: astronauts see only their own data; the Crew Medical Officer also sees a crew overview.

- What-if sliders (exercise, sleep, thigh cuffs) show the landing-day body change live.

- Environment switch: Space Station, Mars transit, Moon base, Mars base (changes delay, gravity and radiation).

HOW IT WORKS

Four layers, all running on the device (offline-first, installable, no server): simulation -> engine -> store -> screens. Real astronaut health data is private, so three fictional crew members are simulated day by day with seeded physiology models (no random numbers). Every rate has a source in the code, e.g. bone loss up to 1-1.5% per month (CSA), Mars transit radiation about 1.8 mSv/day (Curiosity RAD, Zeitlin et al., Science 2013), NASA's 600 mSv career limit. 103 automated tests check the science rules.

BENEFITS

It makes a 20-minute delay manageable: the crew always has a plan, and Earth gets a clear, prioritized report.

TOOLS

React, TypeScript, Vite, Recharts, Vitest, vite-plugin-pwa, Vercel, GitHub.

Prototype for education. Not a medical device. Simulated crew data.
